Searched extensively (Russian + Ukrainian) for any 2024-2026 news specific to the Soyuz line and to the Sokhranivka crossing it uses. Findings, newest first: (1) biz.liga.net, 2025-01-01: the entire 2019 Russia-Ukraine transit agreement expired unrenewed at 07:00 on 2025-01-01, ending ALL remaining gas transportation from Russia's Sudzha entry point westward through Ukraine — the last live transit route in the system Soyuz belongs to. (2) A neftegaz.ru news item (2024, headline 'Applications for Russian gas transit via Ukraine's GTS fell 25%. However, Sokhranovka...') indicates Gazprom was still filing daily nomination requests at the Sokhranivka station through 2024 and Naftogaz was rejecting them — i.e., ZERO flow via Soyuz's own entry point continuously since May 2022, well before the 2025-01-01 full stoppage. (3) ru.wikipedia and multiple corroborating sources confirm the Sokhranivka GIS — Soyuz's sole Russia→Ukraine crossing — has been shut to transit since May 2022 because it sits in Russian-occupied Luhansk territory. Net effect: Soyuz has carried no Russia-to-Ukraine transit gas since May 2022 (over 4 years), and the broader corridor it feeds has been formally dead since 2025-01-01. This is squarely 'mothballed' (physically intact, not decommissioned, simply unused for its transit function amid the war) rather than 'operating' (no current flow) or 'retired' (no evidence of decommissioning/dismantling — the standing country guidance explicitly warns against inferring retirement from the general transit-halt fact alone, and I found no line-specific decommissioning evidence). I did not find any indication Soyuz still moves domestic Ukrainian or reverse-flow gas on its Ukraine section independent of the Russia-sourced transit function, so I'm confirming the existing status as-is rather than proposing a change.

No source describes any gas flow or plan to restore one; Russia-Ukraine transit ended entirely 2025-01-01 per the country's standing context, further reinforcing there is no live use case for this Russia->Ukraine import line. 'Mothballed' (idle, not formally decommissioned) remains a defensible read since I found no formal retirement declaration by either Gazprom or the Ukrainian side — but the case for upgrading to 'retired' is real and building: the compressor station was already being liquidated pre-war (2020), the whole transit relationship it once served ended 2025-01-01, and the pipe itself is now being deliberately destroyed/flooded as war damage. Flagging this combination for the Update leg to weigh a Status change to 'retired' rather than proposing it here without a direct decommissioning declaration.

ENTSOG's TRA-N-502 pipeline table gives the Ukrainian-part pipe as 700 mm. 700/25.4 = 27.5591 in, which rounds to 27.56 in, not the sheet's 27.60 in — a small but real discrepancy consistent with someone typing a rounder-looking number instead of converting precisely. Recommend correcting to 27.56 in (or storing 700 mm directly) and citing the source. LENGTH (30 km) matches TRA-N-502's table exactly ('Ukrainian part... Length (km) 30'). CAPACITY (7.70 MMSCMD): ENTSOG lists the capacity increment at the Siret(RO)/Khotyn(UA) point as 58.10 GWh/d (RO->UA) and 87.10 GWh/d (UA->RO). Converting GWh/d to MMSCMD with the standard ~11 kWh/Sm3 gas heating-value convention gives roughly 5.3 and 7.9 MMSCMD respectively -- the sheet's 7.70 MMSCMD sits within ~3% of the UA->RO (export) figure, which is a reasonable match given the conversion-factor approximation; treated as confirmed, single-source. SEGMENTCOST (40,000,000 EUR) could NOT be corroborated. All cost figures found in Transgaz's own planning documents (125M EUR in the 2018-2027 plan, 150M EUR in 2021-2030, 450M EUR in the new 2026-2035 plan) price the much longer 130-146 km ROMANIAN section (Gheraesti-Siret), a different segment/different GEM entity -- applying any of those numbers to this 30 km Ukrainian spur would be wrong.
